reader_summary: Handing over an assistant means naming the compatible base, text/image processing tools, recognizer and chosen settings, plus an optional LoRA only when actually selected. A SHA-256 check answers whether the received bytes match the manifest; running the interface answers whether the route works; a capability card answers which complete tasks passed. The selected release keeps Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct and Whisper-large-v3-turbo with LoRA off. Its final test supports limited photo and Chinese text-reading uses while showing weak chat, action description and reading-order performance. Neither transcription accuracy nor an ended response proves successful assistance, and a new or changed use needs its own complete-task evaluation.

background_and_links.details: The section names 19.11 and 20.3 as prerequisites. Reading them supplied the inference-versus-resume distinction and the base/optional-repair/ASR roles. I also used the explicit 20.8 and 20.12 links for validation selection and voice-route responsibility, and followed 19.11’s explicit 6.5 tokenizer-pairing link for the meaning of the token budget. I did not search unrelated chapters. The final-score/configuration/public-release links are clearly cited records, and the student/data/training links are next actions; reading those records or executing their workflows is not necessary for this section’s exercise.

terminology.details: Version is a specified edition; SHA-256 is a deterministic content digest over bytes; a parameter is a stored learned number (20.3); LoRA is an optional small learned correction used with the base, currently disabled; ASR writes the heard words before the chat model responds (20.12). The 6.5 explanation and figure show a token is a tokenizer-dependent text piece, so 384 new tokens is an output budget rather than a promise of 384 characters. CER counts character edit operations divided by source-transcript character count. NFKC is introduced operationally as character-form normalization, with fullwidth digits as an example; subsequent whitespace removal still retains the stated punctuation/case/script distinctions. FLEURS and AISHELL are named source groups with their role and counts explained here, and understanding this card does not require their full dataset histories. One nonblocking OCR whitespace-rule clarification is recorded in issues.

examples.details: The book-and-note analogy explains why a matching correction still needs its specific base; the appliance analogy explains why detecting text and copying it are separate uses. The artificial base A/adapter B versus adapter C bytes differ, so complete digests compare False; equal bytes compare True. I checked the short arithmetic and can account for each table row and its limits in capability_table_understanding. I interpret 178 as generated answers with shared contexts, not independent situations; 171 ended outputs are not 171 correct outputs. The CER denominators are characters, not recordings. No percentages or capability claims were remeasured from model outputs.

program_explanation.details: The only target fence imports hashlib.sha256, sets two artificial bytes values (b prefix), displays the first 12 hexadecimal digest characters via hexdigest()[:12], and compares complete binary digests via digest(). The shortened display is not the equality test or the formal download check. The original offline run displayed 45de0d2401bf and b43173684456 followed by False; my exercise variant sets received = expected and displayed 45de0d2401bf twice followed by True. These are text-byte demonstrations, not a real model-file integrity check. Formal delivery requires the full expected digest plus size and compatible configuration. The assigned section has no shell command or additional code fence; all prerequisite download/training commands were read only.

exercise.details: I predicted and executed the equal-received edit: the final line became True. Equal fingerprints cannot replace a capability card, because identical bytes can still give incorrect or truncated answers. I wrote three new complete multi-turn conversation tasks with explicit messages, preserved/corrected constraints and predeclared end-to-end checks in own-exercise-response.json. They exercise a scope not established by the one failed history-dependent item in the card. These are proposed future tasks, not generated-answer results or a claim of long-conversation reliability.

capability_table_understanding.meaning: 25 of 42 photo prompts passed a one-to-two-sentence Traditional Chinese main-content request; this does not establish exhaustive detail reporting.

58 of 84 questions passed, with two questions on each of the same 42 photos. Action 3/11 and relation 21/29 are subsets inside 84, not extra test questions; their difference matters for what kinds of scene facts are reliable.

capability_table_understanding.use: Visible Chinese text present or absent
capability_table_understanding.meaning: All 18 presence decisions passed: 10 with and 8 without clearly visible Chinese. Detecting presence does not show exact reading.

8 of 10 photo-region tasks passed. Original Traditional/Simplified forms and punctuation matter, with a prescribed whitespace treatment; the task does not transcribe all text on each photo. Exact whitespace treatment is my small open clarification.
Only 1 of 3 passed; content and requested sequence/newlines must both be correct. Three selected-region tasks do not establish general full-page layout understanding.

2 of 13 passed, with seven truncated answers still counted in the denominator. Only one item required previous conversation and it failed, so this is insufficient evidence for long multi-turn assistance.

22 read-aloud Mandarin clips: 18 FLEURS statements and four AISHELL questions. Raw edit count 112 over 674 reference characters is 16.62%; after the stated normalization, 96 over 661 is 14.52%. This is CER, not a fraction of successful conversations. FLEURS contributes 112/632 raw and 96/619 normalized, while AISHELL contributes 0/42 to both; the counts and denominators add consistently.
Two of the same four AISHELL questions passed when the chat core received the correct source transcript, isolating its answer responsibility.

Two of those four questions also passed through the actual audio transcription route. All four questions having zero transcription edits does not mean four successful answers; both answer routes still require judging complete responses.

formula_and_numbers.cer: CER = (insertions + deletions + substitutions) / number of reference transcript characters. Reference size is recomputed under the chosen raw or normalized text convention; error count is not the number of wrongly heard recordings.
formula_and_numbers.model_parameters: 2,127,532,032 belongs to the chosen visual-language base; 808,878,080 belongs to the separate recognizer. These do not turn recognizer performance into evidence of LoRA improvement; LoRA is off in the selected configuration.
formula_and_numbers.answers_and_stopping: 42+84+18+10+3+13+4+4 = 178 generated answers; 171 ended + 7 truncated = 178. The ASR CER row is a separate character-error measurement. The seven truncations used their 384-new-token allowance without a normal ending, and remain in the 13-chat-task denominator.
formula_and_numbers.pass_rule: Passing requires meeting the prior content rubric, following the user request and ending normally. Normal ending alone is insufficient. Shared photographs and shared voice questions prevent treating 178 as 178 independent settings or forming an unrestricted overall score.
